items.title: Daemon IPC, lifecycle, state CLI and redaction
items.stop_rule: Do not proceed while a concurrent starter can unlink a live socket or peer validation is weaker than Go.
acceptance: Superseded, not run: cargo clippy ... --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. Native Windows is outside the supported platform scope (AGENTS.md, 2026-10-29, #990).
items.native_evidence_gate: .github/workflows/browse-daemon-native.yml on ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm and macos-15 (Windows and macOS Intel left the platform scope, #990): the daemon unit and integration tests, the 50x50 competing-start race, the lifecycle suite, the sealed state-key replay (31 startup cases) and, since 2026-11-13, the sealed registry replay (510 CLI observations, 20 raw frames, 8 concurrent clients, 12 root-prefix --session observations) and process replay (84 daemon requests) run against the release binary; raw logs and receipts are uploaded. Go is not run anywhere: the Go side is read from recordings pinned by retention.json or by sha256, and a changed, missing or unregistered recording fails before any case runs.
items.remaining_scope: Complete; no blocking scope. Rust-only evidence replaces the removed live Go oracle (maintainer decision 2026-11-09). (1) Native state-key replay: workflow run 42919403688 on main 5cfb54c46 is green on ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm and macos-15 (31/31 startup pairs, 3/3 controls, store probe); independent full review of that replay was done and its four findings fixed. (2) 2026-11-13 local receipts (base 3c9c4ff9c plus this change; migration/evidence/browse-daemon-772/rust-only-replay-receipt-20261113.json): macOS arm64 and Linux arm64 (rust:1.98.0-bookworm container) match the sealed registry recording (510/510 CLI observations, 20 frames, 8 clients, 10 controls rejected), the 12 root-prefix --session observations (12/12, 3 controls rejected) and the process recordings (macOS 42+21 requests, Linux 63+21, 3 controls each; on macOS three Linux-only cases are platform-unavailable and are not counted as parity). (3) Rust fixes found by the replays, each with a regression test: non-UTF-8 argv was lossy-converted (session_argv.rs), state clean --output yaml printed null instead of [] (registry replay), the daemon accepted a JSON array as a frame and rejected a whitespace-only cmd (frame_limits.rs, protocol.rs). The root-prefix --session spelling gap is closed. (4) Acceptance on macOS arm64: cargo test -p symbrowse-daemon --locked 82 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored; run.py --suite daemon and --suite daemon-races --repeat 50 pass; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings clean; cargo test --workspace --locked 430 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored over 77 summaries; validate.py ok. Linux arm64 container: symbrowse-daemon tests (frame_limits 5/5, lifecycle 7/7), session_argv 4/4. Not covered: the new registry/process replay steps have not yet run on GitHub Actions (x86_64 Linux in particular), DMN-002 keeps the documented known_gap (Go encoding/json message texts, case-insensitive keys), DMN-003 cannot exercise a foreign-UID peer without a second account, and Windows is out of scope. Unix-socket tests need a short TMPDIR (macOS sun_path limit); launchers with a long TMPDIR fail them for environmental reasons only.

items.title: Static DOM, rendering, relevance, cache and recovery
items.stop_rule: Do not select a renderer until the complete corpus passes; unexplained byte differences are not normalizable.
acceptance: 2026-11-13 macOS arm64 (base de2989174): python3 port/harness/run.py --suite fetch-render --comparison bytes passes (render_corpus 1/1 over 28 vectors, static_controls 5/5, pipeline_controls 8/8); cargo nextest run -p symbrowse-fetch --locked = 91/91 passed. No byte difference exists: no Rust renderer change was needed.

Corpus provenance re-proven 2026-11-13: the pre-removal Go generator scripts/rust-port/fetch_fixture_gen.go and internal/fetch tree from dde8cced1^ were rebuilt (go 1.27.4) and re-run; the regenerated static.json has identical oracle_commit, source_digest 4924c029...50ac1, vector_count 28 and value-identical JSON for every field of all 28 vectors. Raw bytes differ only in how Go spells U+FFFD in JSON strings (the committed file mixes escaped and literal forms); the Rust test compares parsed values, so no normalization of rendered output is involved.

Native receipt: 'Browse honest fetch native contracts' run 42919403496 on main 5cfb54c46 runs cargo test -p symbrowse-fetch --all-targets --locked (includes render_corpus, static_controls, pipeline_controls) green on ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm and macos-15.

items.title: Safari attach and BiDi adapters
items.stop_rule: Keep Safari cfg-gated; stop if the port adds a privilege or installation contract.
items.remaining_scope: 2026-11-08 macOS arm64: Safari attach/BiDi and Firefox unit and contract tests pass. Safari needs Remote Automation on the user's real Safari, which an agent must not drive (maintainer gate). 2026-11-09 Firefox native gate (no geckodriver; the adapter launches Firefox with BiDi directly): the adapter now owns a fresh browsingContext.create tab because Firefox 159 rejects evaluation in the first context of a new profile ("System access is required"); the symbrowse-firefox-spike gate passes on macOS arm64 against Firefox 159.0.1 for a fresh blank tab and a loopback http navigation. .github/workflows/browse-firefox-native.yml runs the same gate on Linux amd64 and macOS; its receipt is pending. Firefox native gate receipt: browse-firefox-native.yml green on linux-amd64 and darwin-arm64; local re-run 2026-11-10 on macOS arm64 against Firefox 159.0.1 passes (unit tests 2/2, blank-tab and loopback-navigation spike, production-daemon firefox_native test 1/1). Firefox BiDi is therefore advertised on macOS and Linux only (symbrowse-core advertise module: --engine validation, daemon capabilities handshake; typed engine_not_advertised elsewhere). Safari is NOT advertised and stays cfg-gated: its native gate needs Remote Automation on the user's real Safari, a maintainer step. Item stays in_progress until that Safari gate passes.

items.title: Fuzzing, mutation, dependency and unsafe hardening
items.remaining_scope: 2026-11-14 macOS arm64 (rustc 1.98.0, nightly 1.101.0-nightly 2026-10-29), evidence in docs/rust-port/hardening.md. All acceptance commands exit 0 after fixes: fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features (435 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored child fixtures; needs a short TMPDIR, see hardening.md), doc tests, cargo hack --each-feature (10/10), scoped Miri via scripts/rust_miri.sh (5/5 properties, 3/3 daemon protocol), cargo audit and --file fuzz/Cargo.lock (no vulnerabilities), cargo deny check and the fuzz manifest (ok, no ignores; the fuzz run needs --config ../deny.toml), scripts/rust_geiger.sh (239 packages, owned unsafe 0, 145 third-party packages with unsafe triaged by category), scripts/fuzz_smoke.sh (7 targets x 4096 runs, seed digests unchanged), fuzz_corpus_hashes.py --check (85 seeds), rust_hardening_inventory.py --write/--check (295 production packages, 0 owned unsafe). Findings fixed: owned unsafe (std::env::set_var) in daemon chrome_native/oracle_replay tests replaced by a re-executed isolated child process plus deny(unsafe_code); only dom-input was fuzzed, so daemon-mcp-frames, flow-yaml, state-headers, urls, fetch-text and http-body-decode targets with seeds, digest manifest and stable replays were added; the referenced scripts and security/rust-hardening-inventory.json did not exist and were created; fuzz/Cargo.toml path dependencies lacked versions (cargo-deny wildcard) and now pin =0.0.0. Reviewed and unchanged: validate_name accepts C1 control characters. Still open: status stays blocked because RUST-015 depends on RUST-013 and RUST-017, whose Safari native gate is a pending maintainer step; no rust-ci.yml/rust-hardening.yml workflow runs these gates yet; h2, httparse and tungstenite are not fuzzed directly; transitive unsafe is accepted per category, not line by line.
items.stop_rule: No owned unsafe code, untriaged advisory/license violation or unfuzzed untrusted parser reaches cutover.
